result.model_name: Kimi (Moonshot AI) — quant trading system architecture review, FTSeek-US round 3

chain_defects.description: Documented but UNFIXED: playbook close-path pnl is never fed into DrawdownController, so the 3% daily-loss brake only sees mainline closes. The worst trade in the dataset (BREAKEVEN_STOP -6035, 81% of total net loss) sits in the playbook-style cohort — i.e. the daily drawdown guard was structurally blind to exactly the flow that needed it. Six daily-loss defenses coexist (header registry) with inconsistent coverage; RiskCircuitBreaker's block action is explicitly 'never wired'.
chain_defects.evidence: Header comment: '已知残留缺口 (未修, 见 DEB P1-M3): playbook 平仓 pnl 未喂入本控制器, 日回撤池当前仅主线平仓在喂 (order_executor C4 点)'. Stats: single-trade loss -6035 vs total -7429.
chain_defects.fix: Add one hook in the playbook close path calling DrawdownController.record_trade_pnl (mirror order_executor C4), plus an integration test asserting both stacks feed the same daily pool. Effort S, do before any capital increase.

chain_defects.description: Capital caps are still observe_only=True: try_reserve '永远返回 True'. There is also no per-trade dollar-risk cap anywhere in the shown sizing path — quantity is not derived from (entry - initial_sl). Result: a single position lost $6,035 while the entire 115-trade sl_hit cohort lost $3,702. Position-level tail risk is currently unbounded by the allocator.
chain_defects.evidence: Code comment: 'Phase B 剩余项: observe_only 切为 False'. Stats: BREAKEVEN_STOP -6035 = 1.6x the whole sl_hit cohort.
chain_defects.fix: Independent of the observe flag, add a hard per-trade risk budget at order sizing: qty <= risk_usd / abs(entry - initial_sl), risk_usd = e.g. 0.5% equity. Then flip observe_only=False bucket-by-bucket.

chain_defects.description: Two config blocks govern the same pre-close behavior with divergent parameters (window_minutes 8 vs default 10; loss_flat=false vs loss_exit min_loss_atr=99/close_ratio 0.0). The file self-declares as SSOT yet contains two sources for one rule. Behavior on the ground contradicts both: PRE_CLOSE_EXIT cohort is 77.3% losers with avg -0.11% even though both blocks describe winners-only closing (loss_flat=false, loss_exit close_ratio 0.0). Either a consumer reads the wrong block or the label is applied to non-pre-close forced exits.
chain_defects.evidence: yaml blocks pre_close_exit{loss_flat:false} and pre_close{loss_exit:{close_ratio:0.0}}; stats PRE_CLOSE_EXIT 22 trades, WR 22.7%, avg_pct -0.11.
chain_defects.fix: Merge to a single block, delete the other, add a startup assert that exactly one consumer key exists; audit which code path stamps exit_reason='PRE_CLOSE_EXIT'.

chain_defects.description: (a) Grace period (45 min) allows only circuit_breaker/earnings_guard/pre_close/atr_stop — trailing/breakeven cannot arm or fire in the first 45 min. Scalping is 129/265 trades (49%) with sub-hour holds: the fastest cohort is structurally denied profit protection during its entire life, which mechanically contributes to the 0.44pp giveback. (b) exit_rules_exclusivity: pre_close mutually excludes trailing_stop, so in the final window winners lose their trailing protection exactly when mean-reversion-into-close risk is highest.
chain_defects.evidence: allowed_during_grace list; exclusivity map pre_close:[trailing_stop, time_exit]. Stats: TRAILING_STOP avg hold 2.4h (only post-grace trades ever trail); overall giveback 0.44pp.
chain_defects.fix: Allow profit-protective arming (breakeven/trailing ratchet updates, even if exit execution is deferred) during grace for positions >+0.5%; remove trailing_stop from pre_close exclusivity and let the quality scorer arbitrate.

chain_defects.description: ExitPolicy.evaluate() performs a synchronous sqlite3.connect + query per position per scan cycle — blocking I/O inside an asyncio exit chain, adding latency precisely on the exit path. No arbitration between this policy layer (CLOSE/REDUCE decisions, priority 8-10) and PositionExitMonitor's rule engine is visible in the provided context: if both fire in the same cycle there is a double-sell race (position could flip short). Also, thesis lookup depends on async thesis_inferer having already written trade_attribution; lag silently degrades to NO_ACTION, so thesis rules (BREAKOUT_FAILED -0.5%, REVERSION_QUICK_PROFIT) apply inconsistently. EVENT_HORIZON_48H reads position.holding_hours — an attribute the stats show is frequently NULL (5 of 9 exit reasons have avg_hold_h None), so this rule may be silently dead. Needs verification: who calls evaluate() and is there a shared per-position exit lock.
chain_defects.evidence: Code: per-call sqlite3.connect in _read_entry_thesis; getattr(position,'holding_hours',0). Stats: avg_hold_h None on sl_hit/time_stop/tp_hit/MOC.
chain_defects.fix: Cache thesis on the position object at open; route all exit decisions through a single per-position lock/arbiter; make holding_hours a required, always-populated field.

chain_defects.description: Two modules each claim to be the single source of truth for stops: StopLossConfig ('止损配置 Single Source of Truth / 全局唯一 SoT', regime defaults -3% to -8%) vs exit_policy.yaml ('唯一真相源', ATR 2.0x capped 2%). Entry-time initial SL and monitor-time SL can therefore be computed from different doctrines; the atr_stop 'floor' contract (min with initial_sl) hides the divergence instead of resolving it. Readers cannot tell which value bound any historical trade.
chain_defects.evidence: Both file headers; stop_loss_config defaults -0.03/-0.08 vs exit_policy max_loss_pct 2.0 and bucket overrides down to 0.3%.
chain_defects.fix: Declare exit_policy.yaml the only stop SoT; have stop_loss_config consume it for entry-time SL (or deprecate it), mirroring the key-consumption audit already done for the global section.

chain_defects.description: Rule [0] widens SL to 4% for the first 15 min while rule [0.5] tightens SL to 1% within the first 30 min if unrealized profit is insufficient — overlapping windows with opposite SL direction make the effective stop path in minutes 15-30 order-dependent. Separately, OVERNIGHT_GAP_STOP is self-admitted misnamed ('无 gap 校验'), and the stats strongly suggest a real mislabeling incident: the -2.98% BREAKEVEN_STOP trade matches long_horizon overnight_gap_stop_pct=3.0 almost exactly.
chain_defects.evidence: Docstring rules [0]/[0.5]/[2]; horizon_selector DEFAULT_CONFIG long_horizon.overnight_gap_stop_pct=3.0 vs trade avg_pct=-2.98, hold 46.3h, MFE 0.0.
chain_defects.fix: Serialize rules [0] and [0.5] with an explicit boundary (e.g. [0.5] only after minute 15); rename the gap stop; stamp every exit with the rule id that set the active SL (SL lineage) so mislabels are detectable.

chain_defects.description: 60s polling + 120s per-position re-trigger cooldown delays both stop execution and retry-after-failure by up to 2 minutes. Fast-move exits land far past intent: FLASH_EXIT cohort avg -1.69% vs the 1.0x ATR design trigger. The same 60s granularity quantizes the trailing ratchet and is a measurable component of the trailing giveback.
chain_defects.evidence: Config values; stats FLASH_EXIT 4 trades avg_pct -1.69; TRAILING_STOP realized 0.6% vs formula-implied 0.85% at MFE 1.42% (≈0.25pp unexplained by the trailing formula — consistent with scan/slippage).
chain_defects.fix: Reduce cooldown to 30s for loss-side exits; add event-driven (tick/quote-push) evaluation for positions already beyond their SL line instead of waiting for the next scan.

exit_logic_findings.code_location: exit_policy.yaml::exit_rules.atr_stop.vol_bucket_multipliers.low.direction_override (LONG max_loss_pct 0.3, SHORT 0.4) + session_adaptation.path_dependency (0.85x tightening for opening_drive)
exit_logic_findings.root_cause: Both, but the stats localize the failure. The -0.13% average loss (which still includes 11.3% winners) implies a median loss well under 0.3% — the binding stop is the low-vol bucket hard cap (0.3%/0.4%, derived circularly as 1.25x the historical loss median 0.24%), not the headline 2xATR/2%. A stop fitted to the historical loss median guarantees ~half of future losers stop out immediately. avg MFE 0.03% shows these trades never moved favorably AT ALL — entries have zero short-horizon edge (scalping: 129 trades, 16.3% WR), so any noise-band stop converts them to losses. The 0.85x opening-drive tightening compounds it.
exit_logic_findings.proposed_change: (1) Floor the stop distance: effective_stop = max(1.0xATR, 0.6%) regardless of bucket override; delete the median-derived 0.3/0.4 caps. (2) Remove the 0.85x opening-drive tightening. (3) Add a 5-minute entry confirmation in signal_pipeline (e.g. price holding on the entry side of VWAP, using existing _get_vwap_deviation) before releasing the order.
exit_logic_findings.expected_effect: Cutting sl_hit share 43%->30% eliminates ~34 stop-outs x ~$32 = +$1.1K per 265-trade window, plus converts a fraction of survivors into the trailing cohort (76 trades, avg +$58/trade). Secondary benefit: sl_hit winners (11.3%) reveal label pollution — re-stamp ratcheted stops with their true rule.

exit_logic_findings.stat_fact: avg MFE 0.48% vs avg realized 0.04% — 0.44pp giveback per trade
exit_logic_findings.code_location: app/playbook/adaptive_trailing.py:30-72 (defaults target_capture_pct=60.0, min_drawdown_pct=0.4, max_drawdown_pct=1.2; clamp return min(max(dd, min), max))
exit_logic_findings.root_cause: The min_drawdown_pct=0.4 floor mathematically reproduces the observed giveback: drawdown = clamp(0.4 x MFE, 0.4, 1.2). For ANY trade with MFE < 1.0%, the floor binds, forcing exit at MFE - 0.4%. At the dataset's avg MFE of 0.48%: predicted exit = +0.08%; subtract 60s scan-interval slippage ≈ 0.04% — exactly the observed avg realized 0.04%. The leak is not diffuse; it is this one clamp.
exit_logic_findings.proposed_change: Make the floor relative: min_dd = min(0.4, 0.30 x MFE) (or lower the default to 0.15), so a 0.5%-MFE trade is allowed to keep ~0.35% instead of 0.08%. Simultaneously raise target_capture_pct 60->70 for MFE > 1% and use the existing EXT_ADAPTIVE_TRAILING_MAX_DD env hook to trial max cap 1.2->0.8 in shadow.
exit_logic_findings.expected_effect: Overall giveback 0.44 -> ~0.2pp. At the implied average notional (~$24.6K, derived from sl_hit: $32 loss / 0.13%), +0.2pp across 265 trades ≈ +$13K upper bound; conservatively counting only trail+pre-close cohorts, +$4-7K per 265-trade window — enough to flip total pnl positive by itself.

exit_logic_findings.stat_fact: TRAILING_STOP: 76 trades, +4444 (main profit source), WR 39.5%, avg hold 2.4h, MFE 1.42% -> realized 0.6% (58% giveback within winners)
exit_logic_findings.root_cause: The profit engine works but leaks at both ends of MFE: below MFE 1% the 0.4% floor eats 40-80% of the move (see above); at MFE 1.42% the 40% giveback formula yields dd=0.57 -> expected exit 0.85%, yet realized is 0.60% — the residual ~0.25pp is scan-interval + cooldown + market-order slippage. The F3 comment in code already acknowledges the max_clamp saturation (MFE 3% and 16% share the same 1.2% drawdown). The 39.5% WR is acceptable IF capture rises; the cohort is net +$58/trade despite the leak.
exit_logic_findings.proposed_change: Same trailing-floor fix (relative min_dd) + target_capture 70 for MFE>1%; move trailing ratchet evaluation from 60s polling to tick-driven updates for positions with open profit > 0.5%; validate the env-based max-DD override (0.8) in shadow before config change (code explicitly supports it).
exit_logic_findings.expected_effect: Raising capture on this cohort from 0.60% to ~0.95% of MFE adds ~0.3pp x 76 trades x ~$24.6K ≈ +$5.6K per 265-trade window, with no change to entry logic or risk appetite.

exit_logic_findings.stat_fact: STRUCTURE_EXIT: 33 trades, -3305, WR 30.3%, avg hold 0.5h, MFE 0.12%
exit_logic_findings.code_location: exit_policy.yaml::exit_rules.technical_breach.enabled=false (2026-06-21) vs app/strategy/exit_policies.py MainPipelineExitPolicy thesis=='breakout' -> BREAKOUT_FAILED CLOSE at pnl<=-0.005
exit_logic_findings.root_cause: The yaml disable-note cites exactly '33笔 -$3,106' — statistically the same cohort as the 33/-3305 in these stats, so these rows are pre-fix era and the current config does not produce STRUCTURE_EXIT. HOWEVER the same behavior was re-implemented under a new label in the thesis layer: BREAKOUT_FAILED hard-closes at -0.5% with no confirmation, which for US intraday noise is the same false-trigger machine (avg hold 0.5h, MFE 0.12% profile). The rule died; the logic survived.
exit_logic_findings.proposed_change: Segment trade_records by date to confirm zero STRUCTURE_EXIT after 2026-06-21 (if any exist, find the live producer — needs the exit_reason writer map, not in provided context). Soften BREAKOUT_FAILED: require a closed 5-min bar below the breakout level, or widen to -0.8%, before CLOSE.
exit_logic_findings.expected_effect: Prevents re-accumulating the documented -$100/trade structural-loss pattern (~-$3.1K per 33 trades) under the new label; keeps breakout theses alive through normal noise.

exit_logic_findings.stat_fact: BREAKEVEN_STOP: 1 trade, -6035 USD, -2.98%, WR 0%, hold 46.3h, avg MFE 0.0% — while breakeven.enabled=false in the mainline SSOT
exit_logic_findings.code_location: app/playbook/exit_engine.py rules [1] SL_BREAKEVEN / [2] OVERNIGHT_GAP_STOP; app/playbook/horizon_selector.py long_horizon overnight_gap_stop_pct=3.0; mainline exit_policy.yaml breakeven.enabled=false
exit_logic_findings.root_cause: A true breakeven stop is arithmetically incapable of this row: arming requires realized peak profit >= trigger (playbook breakeven_at_pct=0.4%), which mandates MFE >= 0.4% — observed MFE is 0.0%. Three converging clues: (a) magnitude -2.98% ≈ long_horizon overnight_gap_stop_pct 3.0% — smells like an OVERNIGHT_GAP_STOP exit mislabeled BREAKEVEN; (b) 46.3h hold at 0 MFE should have been killed by MFE_STALL_EXIT [3.4] at 150min (peak<0.5%, underwater) — its survival implies either an exemption path (_loser_overnight_exempt/_overnight_eod_exempt imports at module top) or broken peak tracking (peak_price is '从 meta 恢复' — lost on restart, which would also zero MFE); (c) no per-trade dollar cap let one position reach -6035 = 1.6x the entire 115-trade sl_hit cohort.
exit_logic_findings.proposed_change: (1) Add a logging invariant: exit_reason BREAKEVEN requires armed_sl >= entry (LONG) and recorded MFE >= trigger — violation auto-relabels to the actual SL-setting rule and pages an alert. (2) Audit playbook breakeven arming for sign/abs-class bugs (the atr_stop_engine P0-2 header documents exactly this bug class historically) and for meta-restore correctness after restart. (3) Persist peak_price/MFE durably so 46h trades cannot show MFE 0.0. (4) Per-trade max dollar risk at sizing (see chain_defects #2).
exit_logic_findings.expected_effect: Removes single-trade account-killers: this one row is 81% of total net loss; capping it at even 0.5% equity (~$300-500) would have saved ~$5.5K, turning total pnl from -7429 to roughly -1900.

exit_logic_findings.stat_fact: tp_hit: only 5/265 trades (1.9%) despite avg MFE 0.48% exceeding the low-bucket take_profit_pct 0.4%
exit_logic_findings.root_cause: The bucket take_profit_pct keys look like the same 'decorative knob' pattern the yaml itself documents for the global section ('写了不代表生效'): the only partial-TP machinery (scale_out) is disabled, and playbook TP requires RR>=1.5. So for the majority of trades there is NO active profit-taking exit — winners can only leave via trailing (with the leaky floor), pre_close, or SL. This is a structural contributor to the MFE->realized gap.
exit_logic_findings.proposed_change: Audit consumers of take_profit_pct (same key-by-key method as the 2026-08-28 census). If unwired, wire a single-tier reduce-only limit TP (50%) at the bucket level; gate activation on replay showing it beats letting the trailing stop run.
exit_logic_findings.expected_effect: Converts part of the 0.48% avg MFE into locked profit on trades that currently round-trip; sign is uncertain (caps some future trail winners) — hence replay-gated. Needs verification of consumer map before sizing the effect.

profit_proposals.title: Fix the adaptive-trailing 0.4% drawdown floor (the giveback clamp)
profit_proposals.change: In adaptive_trailing_drawdown_pct: min_dd = min(0.4, 0.30*MFE) (or config default adaptive_trailing_min_drawdown_pct 0.4->0.15); target_capture_pct 60->70 for MFE>1%; shadow-trial EXT_ADAPTIVE_TRAILING_MAX_DD=0.8
profit_proposals.expected_impact: Floor alone reproduces the observed 0.44pp giveback (MFE 0.48 - 0.4 floor - slippage = realized 0.04). Halving giveback to ~0.2pp is worth +$4-7K per 265-trade window (trail cohort +$5.6K at +0.3pp capture) — the single highest-EV change; total pnl -7429 flips positive.
profit_proposals.validation_method: Replay: re-run the 265 closed trades' MFE/peak paths through the modified trailing function offline (pure function, no I/O by design); then 2-week shadow via existing harness/shadow_bridge (config/exit_profiles.yaml) before config flip.

profit_proposals.title: Shadow-disable the scalping strategy pending edge re-validation
profit_proposals.change: Config flag to route scalping signals to shadow-only (log-only, no orders) for 2 weeks; keep voting_llm live. Scalping: 129 trades, 16.3% WR, -3511.
profit_proposals.expected_impact: If scalping's era-adjusted expectancy is still negative, direct saving equals its loss rate (-3511 per 265-trade window, ~-$27/trade). Zero-execution-risk way to test: shadow log reveals whether its signals would have recovered under the fixed trailing.
profit_proposals.validation_method: Shadow A/B via existing shadow_bridge; compare shadow scalping pnl (with fixed trailing params) vs live voting_llm over the window; also segment scalping pnl by date to rule out pre-fix-era contamination.

profit_proposals.title: Stop-distance noise floor + 5-minute entry confirmation
profit_proposals.change: exit_policy.yaml: replace low-bucket direction_override max_loss_pct 0.3/0.4 with effective floor max(1.0xATR, 0.6%); remove session_adaptation 0.85x opening-drive tightening; signal_pipeline: add 5-min post-signal confirmation (price on entry side of VWAP via existing _get_vwap_deviation) before order release
profit_proposals.expected_impact: sl_hit share 43%->~30%: ~34 fewer stop-outs x $32 = +$1.1K direct, plus survivors converting into the trailing cohort (+$58 avg). Also fixes the circular median-fit that guarantees ~50% immediate stop-outs in the low-vol bucket.
profit_proposals.validation_method: Replay the 115 sl_hit trades against 1-min bars with the widened stop: count how many would have survived to reach their recorded MFE vs stopped; requires intraday bars (MAE is not logged — see data_consistency_issues). Then shadow A/B config.

profit_proposals.title: Breakeven-exit invariant + per-trade dollar risk cap
profit_proposals.change: exit_engine: invariant check at exit logging (BREAKEVEN implies armed_sl>=entry and MFE>=trigger, else relabel+alert); order sizing: qty <= risk_usd/abs(entry-initial_sl) with risk_usd=0.5% equity, independent of CapitalAllocator observe_only; persist peak_price/MFE durably
profit_proposals.expected_impact: Tail-risk removal, not expectancy: the -6035 trade was 81% of total net loss and 1.6x the entire sl_hit cohort. Capping at 0.5% equity saves ~$5.5K on that single event class; the invariant converts silent mislabels into alerts.
profit_proposals.validation_method: Unit tests for the invariant and sizing formula; replay the specific 46.3h trade's quote path to identify which rule actually fired; shadow-enforce the dollar cap for 1 week (log would-have-been-blocked sizes).

profit_proposals.title: Feed playbook realized pnl into DrawdownController (close the documented blind spot)
profit_proposals.change: Single hook in playbook close path calling DrawdownController.record_trade_pnl (mirror order_executor C4 point), + integration test asserting both stacks contribute to the same daily pool
profit_proposals.expected_impact: Does not add profit directly; makes the 3% daily-loss brake real for the stack that produced the -6035 day. Prevents multi-thousand-dollar days from compounding undetected — expected value is avoided tail days, not per-trade alpha.
profit_proposals.validation_method: Integration test + 1 week observe-mode logging comparing the six daily-loss defenses' views before relying on enforcement.

profit_proposals.title: Unify pre-close config and keep trailing armed into the close
profit_proposals.change: Merge exit_rules.pre_close_exit and exit_rules.pre_close into one block (single window, single loss policy); remove trailing_stop from exit_rules_exclusivity.pre_close; audit which code path stamps PRE_CLOSE_EXIT on losing trades (config says winners-only, stats show 77.3% losers)
profit_proposals.expected_impact: Protects the +2263 pre-close cohort's winners from un-trailed reversal in the last 15 min and stops loser exits from hiding under the PRE_CLOSE_EXIT label (data integrity + modest giveback reduction, est. +$0.5-1K/window).
profit_proposals.validation_method: Replay last-30-min paths of the 22 PRE_CLOSE_EXIT trades with trailing left armed; config-load test asserting single pre-close block.

profit_proposals.title: Wire the bucket take_profit_pct as reduce-only limit orders (replay-gated)
profit_proposals.change: Census consumers of vol_bucket take_profit_pct (currently likely decorative since scale_out is disabled); wire a single-tier 50% reduce-only limit TP at the bucket level behind a config flag; consider low-bucket TP 0.4->0.6 given avg MFE 0.48%
profit_proposals.expected_impact: tp_hit is currently 1.9% of exits while avg MFE (0.48%) exceeds the low-bucket TP (0.4%) — profit-taking machinery is effectively absent. If replay shows locking 50% at TP beats the trailing alternative on sub-1% MFE trades, adds ~+0.1pp on roughly half of trades (~+$3K/window upper bound); sign is uncertain because it caps some future trail winners — hence replay gate.
profit_proposals.validation_method: Offline replay comparison (TP-partial vs trailing-only) on the 265-trade MFE paths; A/B config in shadow_bridge for 2 weeks.

data_consistency_issues.observation: BREAKEVEN_STOP row: -2.98%, MFE 0.0%, hold 46.3h, while mainline breakeven.enabled=false
data_consistency_issues.why_suspicious: Semantically impossible: a breakeven stop arms only after peak profit >= trigger (0.4-1.5%), which mandates MFE >= trigger — MFE 0.0% contradicts the label. A 46.3h zero-MFE trade should also have been killed by MFE_STALL_EXIT at 150min. And -2.98% ≈ long_horizon overnight_gap_stop_pct=3.0.
data_consistency_issues.likely_cause: Either an OVERNIGHT_GAP_STOP exit mislabeled BREAKEVEN (rule-id stamping gap), or breakeven armed from corrupted state (peak_price restored from meta lost on restart — which would also explain MFE 0.0), or a sign/abs-class arming bug on a SHORT. Needs the exit_reason writer map and that trade's SL lineage to disambiguate.

data_consistency_issues.observation: PRE_CLOSE_EXIT: avg_pct -0.11 (negative) with total_pnl +2263 (positive) and WR 22.7%
data_consistency_issues.why_suspicious: A negative mean per-trade pct with a large positive dollar total requires extreme size skew (5 winners dwarfing 17 losers) — possible but conspicuous; also the cohort being 77% losers contradicts the winners-only pre-close design (loss_flat=false, loss_exit close_ratio 0.0).
data_consistency_issues.likely_cause: avg_pct computed over a subset (rows with non-null pct), a sign error for SHORT pct, partial closes booked under this reason, or non-pre-close forced exits stamped PRE_CLOSE_EXIT. Verify by recomputing avg_pct and pnl from raw rows.

data_consistency_issues.observation: sl_hit has an 11.3% WIN rate (≈13 profitable 'stop-loss hits')
data_consistency_issues.why_suspicious: An initial stop-loss exit should be a loss by construction; profitable sl_hit rows mean the label is applied to exits at ratcheted/trailed stops or to slippage outcomes, polluting the per-rule statistics this review (and the system's own tuning notes) rely on.
data_consistency_issues.likely_cause: exit_reason stamped from the SL line's origin ('initial') rather than the rule that moved it; missing SL-lineage tracking. Same root cause as the BREAKEVEN_STOP mislabel.

data_consistency_issues.observation: avg_hold_h is NULL for 5 of 9 exit reasons (sl_hit, time_stop, tp_hit, FLASH_EXIT partial, MOC)
data_consistency_issues.why_suspicious: Hold time is a first-class exit-quality dimension (the config's own design rationale is built on hold-bucket stats like '4-24h持仓 70.7%WR'); systematic nulls on specific exit paths mean those paths skip hold-time logging.
data_consistency_issues.likely_cause: Instrumentation gap in the writers for those exit paths (holding_hours not populated at close). Also casts doubt on exit_policies.py EVENT_HORIZON_48H, which reads position.holding_hours — if the same field is null on position objects, that rule is silently dead.

data_consistency_issues.observation: Stats blend multiple config eras: STRUCTURE_EXIT 33 trades (config disabled 2026-06-21 citing exactly '33笔' -$3,106), flash_exit 'removed 2026-06-20' yet 4 trades, time_stop 'DEAD 2026-06-20' yet 7 trades, breakeven disabled 2026-06-28 yet 1 trade
data_consistency_issues.why_suspicious: The STRUCTURE_EXIT count matches the disable note's cohort exactly (33; pnl -3106 vs -3305, minor fee-basis drift) — proving these aggregates are all-time, not current-config performance. Mixed-language labels (MOC 收盘强制平仓 alongside English) reinforce taxonomy drift across eras.
data_consistency_issues.likely_cause: trade_records has no config-version column; per-rule stats are not date-segmented. Any 'is rule X working' question (including this review's) must first filter by rule-active window, or disabled-rule history contaminates current conclusions — e.g. scalping's -3511 may partly predate the fixes.

data_consistency_issues.observation: MFE recorded as 0.0% on a 46.3h trade (BREAKEVEN_STOP) and FLASH_EXIT rows
data_consistency_issues.why_suspicious: A US stock held 46 hours having literally zero favorable excursion is near-impossible; FLASH_EXIT at MFE 0.0 is plausible but the 46h case indicates peak tracking failure.
data_consistency_issues.likely_cause: peak_price is restored from meta and lost on process restart (exit_engine docstring: 'peak_price: 历史峰值价 (从 meta 恢复)'), silently zeroing MFE for positions spanning restarts. Since the entire giveback analysis (0.44pp) depends on MFE integrity, MFE should be persisted transactionally, not reconstructed.

data_consistency_issues.observation: MAE (max adverse excursion) is absent/all-zero in the stats extract
data_consistency_issues.why_suspicious: The key diagnostic for 'stops too tight vs entries too weak' is MFE-MAE joint distribution; with MFE present but MAE missing, stop-tuning decisions (like the circular median-fit bucket caps) are being made one-sided.
data_consistency_issues.likely_cause: MAE never instrumented in the exit/attribution writers (same class of gap as trail_state historically being all-0.0, per position_exit_monitor header). Add MAE capture alongside peak_price.

overall_assessment.summary: Scores on a 0-100 scale. The system does not have an exit-alpha problem so much as an exit-leak and entry-quality problem wrapped in unreliable telemetry. Entries are weak: 43% of all trades die at a stop with 0.03% average MFE (zero initial edge, worst in the scalping cohort at 16.3% WR), and both strategies have negative expectancy — every dollar of profit comes from the exit machinery (TRAILING_STOP +4444, PRE_CLOSE +2263) on a minority of trades. That machinery leaks by construction: the adaptive-trailing 0.4% floor exactly reproduces the observed MFE 0.48% -> realized 0.04% giveback, grace-period and pre-close exclusivity rules disable profit protection for the fastest 49% of trades and for the final window respectively, and bucket take-profit keys appear decorative (tp_hit = 1.9% of exits). Risk containment has structural holes: playbook pnl bypasses the daily drawdown controller (documented, unfixed), capital caps are observe-only, and one mislabeled/anomalous BREAKEVEN_STOP trade (-6035, MFE 0.0, 46.3h) both violates the label's semantics and escaped every time-based kill rule. The statistics reconcile arithmetically but are polluted semantically: era-mixed cohorts (disabled rules still present), mislabeled exit_reasons, null hold-hours, missing MAE, and restart-zeroed MFE. Before any further parameter tuning: fix the trailing floor, instrument SL-lineage + MAE, and date-segment the stats — otherwise the system will keep optimizing against mislabeled history. Context still needed: exit_reason writer map, who invokes ExitPolicy.evaluate() and its arbiter with PositionExitMonitor, the take_profit_pct consumer census, and date-ranged trade rows to separate pre/post-fix eras.
